title: Remembering democratic transitions, the (re-)building of democratic institutions, and strengthening society based on the rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights.
description: Objective: 1. CERV-2026-CITIZENS-REM-TRANSITION - Remembering democratic transitions, the (re-)building of democratic institutions, and strengthening society based on the rule of law, democracy, and fundamental rights. The EU is a community of values, and all its Member States committed to respect the principles of democracy, the rule of law, and respect for fundamental rights . Europe's experiences in the 20th century demonstrates the need for resilient democracies and the need for people to actively engage in and protect democratic institutions and values. Historical experience such as in the 1920s and 1930s, when some European democracies went through particularly challenging times, are stark reminders of the importance to promote democracy, also in a historical perspective. Today, democracy faces several challenges, which underlined the need to strengthen public trust in democratic processes and institutions and to recall the importance of democracy in people’s daily life. Democratic transitions (defined as the transition from a non-democratic to a democratic system, a transition undertaken by several European countries before joining the EU) are not only political and legal processes but also societal transformations.The transition and consolidation of democracies through institutional and legal reforms have been essential. In addition, delivering justice to victims and affected communities after the fall of totalitarian and authoritarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) can aid in societal healing, bolster and reinforce resilience against present and future threats to democracies. Projects under this topic can focus on: The ongoing development and nurturing of democracies in the context of past transitions from authoritarian and totalitarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) across various European countries, reveals important lessons for defending and upholding EU values such as democracy, the rule of law, and fundamental rights. They can also reflect on both shared patterns and national specificities, while underlining the lasting impact of the totalitarian or authoritarian past, and how its difficult legacy continues to be remembered, interpreted, and engaged with today. Examining and giving visibility to acts of resistance and organised opposition to past totalitarian and authoritarian regimes, as part of the ongoing effort to nurture and protect democracy in the face of enduring and emerging challenges. Transition from authoritarian and totalitarian regimes (including communist and fascist dictatorships) towards democracy. Promoting remembrance and education about past events in which fundamental rights such as freedom of expression, assembly, thought, conscience, religion, and electoral rights were suppressed under past totalitarian and authoritarian regimes. These examples serve to reinforce the importance of protecting democratic values today, including the right to express dissenting opinions and ensuring a political space where opposition voices can be freely and safely heard. Exploring the means of historical justice, be it through trials, restitution or amnesty, and possibility still today to work on restorative justice. The elements described above to strengthen democracies, such as fighting foreign interference, including the manipulation and falsification of historical facts, strengthen citizen engagement, critical thinking, media literacy, and societal resilience, are closely related to the context of remembrance, as they help ensure that the dramatic events of the past are not repeated in contemporary Europe. For further information about the call and its conditions, please see the Call document .

title: Innovative tools and business models
description: Objective: The Innovative tools and business models action is aimed at encouraging the development and/or the spread of innovative tools and business models to improve the visibility, availability, audience and diversity of European works in the digital age and/or the competitiveness and/or the greening process of the European audiovisual industry (including videogames). The support also aims to enable the European audiovisual industry to better adapt to the opportunities offered by the development of Artificial Intelligence and contribute to the implementation of the Apply AI Strategy. Expected results Improve the competitiveness of the European audiovisual industry (including videogames) and seize the benefits of the innovative developments in technology and business models; Improve the adaptation of the European audiovisual industry to the opportunities offered by Artificial Intelligence; Improve the greening process of the European audiovisual industry; Improve the production and circulation of European audiovisual works in the digital era; increase the number and diversity of European works available online and increase their visibility in order to allow them to reach more audiences. Description of the activities to be funded The projects can include in particular: Subtitling or accessibility/discoverability/recommendation tools to be widely used across borders and across platforms in order to improve the visibility, the availability and the audience potential of European audiovisual works; Business tools improving the efficiency and the transparency of the audiovisual markets: automated rights management system, technology for data gathering and analysis; Business models seeking to optimise the synergies and complementarities between the distribution platforms (festivals, cinemas, VOD…); Business tools exploring new modes of production, financing, distribution or promotion enabled or enhanced by new technology (AI, big data, blockchain, Virtual worlds / Metaverse, NFT, etc.). Innovative tools and business models improving the greening process of the audiovisual industry. The action does not cover the development of hardware (e.g. cameras, virtual headsets...). Applications should present adequate strategies to ensure more sustainable and more environmentally-respectful industry and to ensure gender balance, inclusion, diversity and representativeness. Transparency plays a key role in the action. Therefore, applications should contain plans for the disclosure of the inputs and results of the action, including among others communicating the results to public authorities, Member States and the audiovisual industry. Special emphasis will also be placed on attracting private investment and on own investment. Project’s ability to apply for a sound and reasonable level of EU public funding below the 80% authorised will be assessed.

description: The Venture Incubation Programme (VIP) serves as an instrument to strengthening incubation capacity in Europe to support early-stage GenAI ventures as well as to: Accelerate the commercialisation of LLM technologies, providing mentoring, access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources, data infrastructures, and regulatory guidance. Promote responsible AI innovation, aligned with the AI Act, Data Act, GDPR, and the EU’s Digital Decade Targets. Foster cross-border collaboration, knowledge sharing, and participation of underrepresented regions and groups in the European AI ecosystem. Through this call, LLM-BRIDGE seeks to identify and support one high-quality, EU-based incubator capable of supporting startups in the transforming of early-stage GenAI ideas into viable, scalable, and ethically compliant ventures that may be eligible to apply for the future Long Jump and European Grand Challenges. Participating in the VIP provides an opportunity for a leading incubator to position itself at the forefront of Europe’s generative AI revolution. This collaboration offers strategic, reputational, and operational advantages, aligning the incubator with a pan-European initiative that seeks to redefine the future of AI-driven innovation and technological leadership. The VIP programme will select one incubator to run a 12-week VIP cohort across Europe, which will: Deliver structured training and mentoring to 30 startups. Provide and facilitate access to technical expertise and AI infrastructures. Monitor and report progress using standardised KPIs defined in the Annex I. Contribute to the overall impact of LLM-BRIDGE and the European GenAI innovation ecosystem. The selected incubator will gain direct access to a carefully selected pipeline of high-potential GenAI startups from across Europe, allowing it to deepen its expertise in nurturing deep-tech ventures with the potential to drive the next wave of generative AI solutions. Such engagement not only enhances the incubators reputation as a leading enabler of cutting-edge innovation but also strengthens its market position within the highly competitive AI ecosystem.

eligibilityText: Proposal submission: All proposals shall be submitted at: https://share.hsforms.com/133VDDomZReqeyGTex0VYRwf4os Proposal template and supporting documents: The proposal template and supporting documents are available at: https://www.llm-bridge.eu/open-calls-2/ Evaluation process: Eligible proposals will be evaluated by independent external experts, appointed by the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium, to ensure objectivity and impartiality. Each proposal will be assessed by at least two experts using the criteria and scoring system defined in the Evaluation Criteria. Applicants will be notified of the evaluation results within four weeks after completion of the panel ranking. Each applicant will receive an Evaluation Summary Report (ESR) containing individual scores, comments, and the final consensus assessment. The successful applicant will be invited to sign a Financial Support Agreement with 28DIGITAL on behalf of the LLM-BRIDGE Consortium. Evaluation criteria: The evaluation is based on the following criteria, each with a maximum score and a minimum threshold: Relevance (maximum score: 10; threshold: 6): Assessment of how well the proposal aligns with the objectives of LLM-BRIDGE, including its capacity to support early-stage Generative AI startups and contribute to European GenAI strategic goals. Track record (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Evaluation of the applicant’s proven experience in incubating and scaling AI or deep-tech ventures, with demonstrated results in terms of startup growth and innovation. Networks and access (maximum score: 8; threshold: 5): Consideration of the ability to provide startups with access to mentors, investors, and strategic industry partners that can strengthen their market positioning and growth potential. Adaptability (maximum score: 6; threshold: 4): Evidence of flexibility and capacity to respond to emerging technological and market needs, particularly in the rapidly evolving Generative AI sector. Monitoring framework (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Quality and clarity of the proposed processes and documentation for monitoring and reporting, including well-defined metrics to track startup progress and overall programme performance. Cost effectiveness (maximum score: 5; threshold: 3): Adequacy and justification of the proposed budget, demonstrating efficient use of resources and value for money. Each criterion is scored from 0 up to its maximum (10, 8, 6 or 5). Proposals are evaluated according to six qualitative levels. Not addressed (score 0 in all scales): The proposal fails to address the criterion or cannot be assessed. Poor (score 1–2 out of 10, 1–2 out of 8, or 1 out of 5/6): The proposal shows serious weaknesses or lacks the required level of detail. Fair (score 3–4 out of 10, 3–4 out of 8, or 2 out of 5/6): Some strengths are present, but significant weaknesses remain. Good – threshold level (score 5–6 out of 10, 5 out of 8, or 3–4 out of 5/6): The criterion is adequately addressed, though moderate weaknesses are observed. Very good (score 7–8 out of 10, 6–7 out of 8, or 4–5 out of 5/6): The criterion is well addressed, with only minor shortcomings. Excellent (score 9–10 out of 10, 8 out of 8, or 5–6 out of 5/6): The criterion is fully addressed, demonstrating outstanding quality with no or only negligible weaknesses. Threshold per criterion: 3 to 6 points. Overall minimum score: 26 points (out of 42). Maximum total score: 42 points. Proposals failing to reach the threshold in any criterion or the overall minimum score will not be considered for funding.

eligibilityText: Applications must be submitted exclusively through the F6S platform ( https://www.f6s.com/trunsport-open-call-1 ) before the deadline specified in the Open Call documentation. Following submission, applications will undergo a multi-stage evaluation process consisting of: 1. Eligibility Check The TRUNSPORT Open Call Management Team will verify compliance with all administrative and eligibility requirements, including: submission before the deadline; completeness of the application; applicant eligibility; Applications failing the eligibility check will not proceed to evaluation. 2. Independent Evaluation Eligible proposals will be evaluated by 2 independent experts with recognised expertise in cybersecurity, critical infrastructures, innovation and digital technologies. Each proposal will be evaluated independently against the evaluation criteria described in the Guidelines for Applicants, covering: Relevance and Objectives; Team Skills and Expertise; Excellence and Implementation; Impact. The maximum evaluation score is 20 points . Minimum threshold scores will apply both per evaluation criterion and overall. 3. Consensus and Ranking Where necessary, evaluators will participate in a consensus process to agree on a final score for each proposal. A ranked list will then be established according to the final evaluation scores. Where proposals receive identical final scores, the tie-breaking procedure described in the Guide for Applicants will be applied. The Evaluation Committee will validate the final ranking list before submitting it for approval by the TRUNSPORT Project Supervisory Board. Results Notification Following completion of the evaluation process, applicants will be informed of the outcome by email. Successful applicants will receive: an Evaluation Summary Report; an invitation to enter the Grant Preparation phase; instructions for signing the Sub-Grant Agreement. Applicants placed on the reserve list will receive: an Evaluation Summary Report; notification of their reserve status. Unsuccessful applicants will receive: an Evaluation Summary Report outlining the evaluation results. Selected beneficiaries will be required to confirm their participation within the deadline specified in the invitation. Failure to respond within the indicated period may result in the offer being transferred to the next eligible applicant on the reserve list. Redress Process Applicants may submit a request for redress if they consider that procedural errors occurred during the eligibility assessment or evaluation process. Requests for redress must: be submitted in writing within the deadline specified in the Guide for Applicants; clearly identify the alleged procedural error; include supporting evidence where appropriate. Redress requests will be examined by the TRUNSPORT Supervisory Board, which was not involved in the original evaluation. The redress procedure is limited exclusively to reviewing the correctness of the evaluation process. It does not involve a re-evaluation of the scientific, technical or operational merits of the proposal. Applicants will be notified of the outcome of the redress procedure by email. All requests for redress should be submitted to the official TRUNSPORT Open Call 1 contact address indicated in the Guide for Applicants.
furtherInformation: Applicants are strongly encouraged to visit the TRUNSPORT website (https://trunsport.eu/open-calls/) and consult the Guide for Applicants, Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) and all supporting documents before preparing and submitting their proposal.

title: Deploying The Network of National Coordination Centres with Member States
description: The aim of the call is to support the creation, development and practical validation of scalable solutions that address the documented needs of the Czech cybersecurity ecosystem. Supported projects must combine design or development, at least one pilot deployment or practical validation, evaluation of results and preparation for further use. The call is focused on three thematic areas: The call is focused on three main thematic pillars: • Scalable solutions for the resilience of small and medium-sized enterprises: new or significantly expanded services and tools to protect small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), self-assessment, prioritisation of measures and sector- specific implementation packages. • Implementation tools and services for compliance readiness, management and risk management: practical solutions for NIS2, CRA, DORA, supply chain security, cybersecurity management, record-keeping, reporting, secure development, SBOM and vulnerability management. • Services and technical solutions for incident preparedness, response and recovery: standardised services, sector-specific scenarios, exercise packages and tools for recovery testing, record-keeping, escalation and reporting. Support will be given primarily to projects that aim to deliver solutions with a measurable impact on a wider target group. Analyses alone, general training or documentation without implementation and validation activities are not a priority. Implementation by individual organisations is eligible primarily as a means of piloting the transferability and wider applicability of the results.
budgetMeaning: Source budget field; not an award or guaranteed per-project amount
eligibilityText: The project proposal will be submitted by the applicant via the application form attached to this call for proposals. The proposal will include the mandatory annexes and any other annexes that the applicants decide to attach in order to demonstrate the eligibility, quality and applicability of the results, the suitability of the proposed mechanism for their application in the context of sustainability, or other parameters of the project. For each project, a member of the NCC-CZ Council will be appointed by the NCC-CZ Council to manage the evaluation process, based on the submission and the sectoral focus of the project. As part of the evaluation, the NCC-CZ administrators will assess the formal compliance of the submitted project proposal with the requirements of the call and will carry out an assessment of the acceptability of the project in terms of the substantive requirements for projects. An independent evaluators will assess the quality and compliance with the material requirements of the projects in accordance with the Terms of Reference of the NCC-CZ and this call. Further information available on: Národní úřad pro kybernetickou a informační bezpečnost - Výzvy
furtherInformation:
In accordance with the programme’s terms and conditions, the maximum amount of financial support is €100,000 and the minimum amount is €60,000 (in the form of a grant),depending on the current exchange rate of the Czech koruna. Projects will be funded at a rate of 50% of eligible costs, which means that the beneficiary will receive funding amounting to one half of the eligible costs incurred during the implementation of the project and substantiated in accordance with the established rules. The funding awarded to a project may be lower than the amount that was requested in the application. The decision on the final amount of support granted will depend on the quality of the project application, the consistency of the expected results with the proposed budget, and the structure of the individual planned costs.

Beneficiaries will be required to regularly provide evidence of actual expenditure incurred in connection with the implementation of the project. Details regarding the frequency and format of reporting will be specified in the grant agreement. Applicants must ensure that the project proposal meets the conditions designed to prevent the project funding from resulting in unauthorised indirect state aid within the meaning of relevant European legislation, or from leading to double funding.

The following types of organisations are eligible to participate in this call and meet the criteria set out in the EU Digital Europe programme:

• Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs).

• Non-governmental organisations (NGOs) that demonstrate professional competence and the ability to produce and practically validate an output in line with the objectives of the call.

• Academic and research institutions are eligible only as members of a consortium that includes at least one small or medium-sized enterprise. They may not submit an application on their own.

Consortia may combine the above-mentioned entities. The application must specify the actual roles, responsibilities and budgets of the members; a formal partnership without evidence of added value is not sufficient.
